rows.sourceExcerpt: Lottery design ranges from a complete draw to a tie-breaker used only among equally ranked candidates. Weighted lotteries give additional chances to groups or applicants with specified characteristics. Weighting can pursue access goals while preserving uncertainty, but it also makes the system harder to explain. If weights are poorly justified, randomisation may conceal rather than resolve disagreement. A draw is therefore not automatically fair; its rules encode values about who enters the pool and whether all entries count alike.
rows.rationale: La proposición afirma «Weighted lotteries can pursue access goals but may be difficult to explain.» y el pasaje dice «Weighting can pursue access goals while preserving uncertainty, but it also makes the system harder to explain.». La fuente conserva la misma relación mediante «pursue», «access», «goals», «explain» y no introduce una condición opuesta; por ello el apoyo es positivo y la clave es YES.

responseBinding.questionText: The passage specifies that every draw must be supervised by a judge.

rows.sourceExcerpt: Trust depends on a published procedure. Applicants should know eligibility rules, the number of available places, whether priority categories exist and how the draw will be checked. Releasing only the final names is insufficient because observers cannot distinguish an honest random process from an arbitrary decision. Independent verification can protect both winners and administrators. Transparency does not remove disappointment, but it changes the basis on which the outcome can be challenged.

El pasaje sí ofrece el contexto «Applicants should know eligibility rules, the number of available places, whether priority categories exist and how the draw will be checked.», pero en el texto completo no especifica «specifies», «supervised» ni afirma lo contrario de la proposición. Por eso la ausencia concreta, y no una contradicción, conduce a NOT GIVEN.

responseBinding.questionText: The author says research value should be the main reason for withholding a place.

rows.sourceExcerpt: A lottery also changes what evaluation can reveal. Because selection among eligible candidates is random, later differences between selected and unselected groups may help researchers study programme effects, provided ethical and methodological conditions are met. Yet evaluation should not become the primary justification for denying a place. The allocation rule must first be defensible to applicants. A post-allocation review should also test whether eligibility and weighting created unintended exclusion.

Esa diferencia verificable niega la relación formulada y justifica NO.

responseBinding.questionText: The preferred allocation method should reflect the institution’s purpose.

rows.sourceExcerpt: No allocation method is universally fair. Queues privilege prompt access, rankings privilege chosen measures, and lotteries privilege an equal or deliberately weighted chance. The appropriate rule follows from institutional purpose and from the kinds of error decision-makers are willing to accept. Where differences in merit are substantial and reliably measured, ranking has a strong claim. Where acceptable candidates are numerous and finely ranked differences are doubtful, randomisation may acknowledge uncertainty more honestly.

responseBinding.questionText: Why does the author distinguish between lotteries used before and after screening?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Because the stage of randomisation changes its fairness implications

rows.sourceExcerpt: When a programme has fewer places than qualified applicants, selection cannot be solved by checking eligibility alone. Every remaining candidate may satisfy the threshold, yet some rule must still decide who enters. A lottery makes chance explicit. Critics see this as surrendering judgement; supporters argue that it can be more honest than pretending to measure tiny differences precisely. Its legitimacy depends on the stage at which it is used. Random admission before basic screening raises a different issue from random selection among candidates already judged suitable.
rows.rationale: La pregunta pide «Why does the author distinguish between lotteries used before and after screening?» y la clave es «Because the stage of randomisation changes its fairness implications». La evidencia dice «Its legitimacy depends on the stage at which it is used.». La coincidencia semántica se apoya en «used», «stage»: esos elementos enlazan el foco de la pregunta y la opción con la información del pasaje, mientras las demás opciones carecen de ese vínculo en el tramo citado.

responseBinding.questionText: What criticism is made of first-come, first-served allocation?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: It can reward advantages unrelated to the programme

rows.sourceExcerpt: First-come, first-served allocation appears neutral because everyone faces the same clock. In practice, it rewards access to time, information and reliable technology. People who learn about an opportunity late, work during registration hours or have unstable internet begin at a disadvantage unrelated to the programme’s purpose. A queue can still be appropriate when early action is itself relevant, but convenience should not be mistaken for fairness. The central question is whether speed of application is a quality the institution intends to reward.

responseBinding.questionText: When might a threshold followed by a lottery be appropriate?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: When acceptable candidates can be identified more reliably than finely ranked

rows.sourceExcerpt: Merit ranking seems to offer the opposite virtue: places go to those judged strongest. The difficulty comes near the cut-off, where small score differences may reflect measurement noise, unequal preparation or subjective assessment. A detailed rank can project false precision. This does not invalidate evaluation. It suggests that a threshold followed by a lottery may be preferable when the institution can distinguish acceptable from unacceptable candidates more confidently than it can order every acceptable candidate.

responseBinding.questionText: Which best summarises bounded randomisation?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: Expert judgement defines the pool and chance resolves the remaining scarcity

rows.sourceExcerpt: The strongest case is for bounded randomisation: judgement defines a defensible pool, and chance resolves scarcity inside it. This model neither eliminates expertise nor treats applicants as identical. It asks experts to make the distinction they can support, then prevents them from inventing confidence beyond that point. Such restraint may feel less decisive than a complete ranking, but decisiveness is not the same as accuracy. A legitimate lottery is not an escape from reasons; it is a rule for acting when reasons run out.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The route should start at the student union. Beginning in the design studio would make the building too familiar to our volunteers.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Across all conditions we keep the same typeface. Otherwise a change attributed to spacing could actually come from letter shape.

responseBinding.questionText: Sound begins when grains move down the ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: The event begins when dry sand avalanches down the steep avalanche face of a dune, whether the movement starts naturally or is triggered carefully.

responseBinding.questionText: The grains tend to occupy a narrow range of ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Booming material often contains grains within a narrow range of grain sizes; a broad mixture does not necessarily move in the same coordinated way.

responseBinding.questionText: The sustained tone has a relatively ______ frequency.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Instead of a sharp crack, observers hear a sustained tone with a relatively low frequency, sometimes lasting while the avalanche continues.

responseBinding.questionText: Too much ______ can prevent the sound.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Dryness matters. Too much moisture between grains can prevent the sound even when the slope and movement look suitable.

responseBinding.questionText: A proposed explanation involves a ______ beneath the surface.

bindings.audiblePhrase: One proposed explanation involves a resonant layer beneath the surface, although its exact role remains debated and should not be presented as settled.

responseBinding.questionText: Field team first records the slope ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: In a field survey, the team first records the slope angle at the active face before disturbing the sand.

responseBinding.questionText: A microphone measures sound ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A calibrated microphone records the sound frequency and its change through time rather than relying on the listener’s description alone.

responseBinding.questionText: Samples are tested for grain size and ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Collected grains are tested for size and roundness, since similar-looking sands may differ in surface form.

responseBinding.questionText: Sensors beneath the surface detect ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Small buried sensors detect vibration beneath the moving surface and show whether oscillation extends into deeper material.

responseBinding.questionText: Competing models are compared with field ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Finally, competing models are compared with field measurements. A plausible mechanism must explain observations at more than one dune.
